purpose: Classify the 2026-09-29 execution-tape disconnects by cause and local hour, and test the stall prediction in agent-report-2026-10-03-trade-stream-coverage.md
mode: read-only; nothing under data/ is written, moved or deleted

excluded: market-day directories dated 2026-09-30 or later (exam panel days)
trades-*, dedupe-*, rejects and global execution_tape_status.json (not lifecycle rows; the global status is current, not dated)
the 88a maker-evidence capture (stream_lifecycle rows), the order book and every other stream

files.why: OPEN/CLOSED gap rows = the lifecycle rows. 09-28 slugs carry the early hours of local 09-29 for markets west of Toronto; 09-26..09-28 give a three-day baseline.
files.expected_size: small: one OPEN and one CLOSED row per route per disconnect, roughly 0.4 KB per row

files.why: per-route last-counted counters (disconnect_count, seconds_dark_completed) to cross-check the classifier totals

option_a_run_in_place.when: 00:30-09:00 local, serially, like any scan on the capture host (it reads a few MB)
option_a_run_in_place.note: Run with the verify worktree as the working directory: the repo-root weather/ shim then resolves to that worktree's src, while from the production clone it would resolve to production src (where this module does not exist) and PYTHONPATH would not override it. A detached worktree does not touch the production working tree, so this rolls nothing. Output goes to scratch/, never data/.

steps: Copy the globs above, preserving the snapshots-relative layout, into one archive outside data/ (e.g. scratch\trade-stream-coverage-20261003\gaps-extract.zip) and record its SHA-256.
Owner moves the archive to the workstation; the workstation agent unpacks it under scratch/ and runs the same command with --snapshots-root pointed at the unpacked folder.

what_to_send_back: disconnects-2026-09-29.json and disconnects-2026-09-28.json (each lists its input files with SHA-256)
the five largest entries of socket_disconnects_by_cause and the daytime_vs_overnight block, pasted into the handback
